extracted.intended_audience: IP professionals, researchers, policymakers, and statisticians
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation and presentation of annual, cross-jurisdictional statistics and indicators for industrial property (patents, utility models, trademarks, industrial designs, geographical indications), including definitions, counting conventions, and normalization methods. Intended to guide interpretation and comparison of IP filing and in-force data across offices and origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary measure: application data
rubrics_metrics.description: This publication focuses primarily on application data, the most often used measure of IP activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use application counts as the principal indicator of IP activity when comparing filing volumes across jurisdictions. The report draws figures from the WIPO Statistics Database and World Intellectual Property Indicators. Note that data are subject to continual updating and may differ from previously published figures or those on WIPO web pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark class count
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark application data refer to class counts – that is, the number of classes specified in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class count affords better international comparison because some jurisdictions allow multiple classes in a single application while others require separate applications per class. Use class counts rather than application counts to compare trademark filing intensity across offices with multi-class vs single-class systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design count (design count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial design data refer to design counts, that is, the number of designs contained in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design count is used to compare filing activity across offices because some offices allow multiple designs in one application and others allow only one. Under the Hague System, a single application may contain up to 100 designs for the same class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Growth means annual growth, that is, the change from 2022 to 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting growth percentages, compute as the year‑on‑year change between the indicated calendar years. Ensure consistent year selection across series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference year and data updating note
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise stated, all data refer to activity that occurred in calendar year 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because statistics are continually updated, figures in this publication may differ from previously published figures and those available on WIPO web pages. Always check the source and date (WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024) when comparing numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident application (statistical definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: For statistical purposes, a resident application refers to an application filed with the IP office of, or acting for, the state or jurisdiction in which the first named applicant in the application is resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resident applications are sometimes called domestic applications. Use the residence of the first named applicant (or assignee in some jurisdictions such as the US) to determine origin for statistical tabulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application abroad (statistical definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application abroad: For statistical purposes, an application filed by a resident of a given state or jurisdiction with the IP office of another state or jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the distinction from a 'non-resident application' (which is from the receiving office's perspective). Use these definitions consistently when aggregating resident vs abroad filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin (country or region) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin of an application means the country or territory of residence of the first named applicant in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some jurisdictions determine origin differently (e.g., the United States uses residence of the assignee in some cases). Be aware of such jurisdictional exceptions when comparing origin-based statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: In force (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: In force refers to IP rights that are currently valid or, in the case of trademarks, active.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To remain in force, IP protection must be maintained (renewal/maintenance obligations). Use 'in force' counts to estimate active stocks of IP rights but consider renewal behavior and jurisdictional differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent (definition used in report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent: A set of exclusive rights granted by law to applicants for inventions that are new, non-obvious and commercially applicable. A patent is valid for a limited period (generally 20 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent system requires full disclosure enabling others skilled in the art to replicate the invention. Use the report's patent definition when interpreting patent application and in-force numbers; be mindful of national differences in patentability criteria and term length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model (definition used in report)
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model (UM) is a special form of patent right. It has less stringent requirements than a patent but gives a shorter term of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models are not available in every jurisdiction. When comparing patent-family style indicators, separate utility model counts or otherwise account for their presence because they represent a different protection instrument with distinct requirements and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical indication (GI) definition and function
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication (GI) is a sign identifying a good as originating in a specific geographical area and possessing a given quality, reputation or other characteristic essentially attributable to that geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main function of a GI is to identify goods while informing about the connection between quality/characteristic/reputation and territory of origin. When aggregating GIs across authorities, beware double counting due to multilateral/bilateral agreements and regional systems (e.g., EU, Lisbon System).

rubrics_metrics.name: Double counting caution for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall total of GIs in force will inevitably include a degree of double counting, as GIs in force through bilateral, plurilateral or multilateral agreements could potentially be included multiple times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If GIs in force through international agreements are excluded, a lower deduplicated total is obtained (report example: excluding such GIs gives ~23,400 instead of ~58,600). Do not sum national/regional GI counts naively without accounting for overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-five offices / share-of-world filings metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage shares of total filing activity by the top five offices (e.g., patents, trademarks, designs) are used to show concentration of filing activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute shares of the world total by office and report trends over time; interpret changes considering rapid growth in some offices (e.g., China) that can alter global concentration measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident applications per USD 100 billion GDP (normalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident patent applications per USD 100 billion GDP: a normalization to compare filing intensity relative to economic size (GDP in 2021 US PPP dollars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this per-GDP normalization to compare countries of different sizes and filing systems. The report includes selection thresholds (e.g., include origins with GDP > USD 25 billion PPP and >100 resident patent applications). Ensure consistent GDP base year (2021 PPP) when reproducing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application class count per USD 100 billion GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident trademark application class count per USD 100 billion GDP: a normalization for trademark filing intensity adjusted for class-count measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection criteria may be applied (e.g., GDP > USD 575 billion PPP and resident class count ≥ 46,000). This metric helps compare countries despite differences in single-class vs multi-class systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design count per USD 100 billion GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident application design count per USD 100 billion GDP: a normalization to compare industrial design filing intensity relative to economic size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Origins were selected based on top application design counts and GDP data availability. Use constant 2021 US PPP dollars for GDP to replicate ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting conventions for classes, designs, and international systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Application class count is the sum of classes specified in applications filed by applicants plus, where applicable, those specified in designations made via the Madrid System. Application design count is the sum of designs contained in applications filed by applicants plus, where applicable, those contained in designations made via the Hague System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Madrid/Hague designations when computing class/design counts. This ensures that international filings made via WIPO-administered systems are captured in origin-based counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes on incomplete origin data / reporting coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Application by origin data are incomplete because some IP offices did not report their resident data in 2023 or provide a detailed breakdown of the origin of applications received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat origin-based tables as best-available estimates and consult statistical table notes. Use caution when comparing origins with missing or partial reporting; the report uses '..' to indicate zero, not available, or not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry / technology field classification metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Top three technology fields (for patents) and top three industry sectors (for trademarks and designs) are reported using classifications (e.g., technology fields, Nice Classification for trademarks, Locarno classes aggregated into sectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified classification systems (e.g., Nice, Locarno, WIPO/EPO PATSTAT mapping) and clearly state the classification period (e.g., 2020–2022) and data sources when reporting sectoral/technological concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design term of protection note
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of protection for industrial design registrations is usually 15 years in most jurisdictions; however differences exist, notably in China (which provides for a 10-year term from the application date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing 'designs in force' or stocks of design rights, account for variation in design term lengths across jurisdictions which affects in-force totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of WIPO IP Statistics Data Center and IP Statistical Country Profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: The WIPO IP Statistics Data Center and IP Statistical Country Profiles are free online services for accessing WIPO statistics on patents, utility models, trademarks, industrial designs and the use of the PCT, Madrid and Hague Systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and policymakers should use these tools to access time series and tailor indicators. The Data Center and Country Profiles are available in multiple languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, Spanish).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation conventions in statistical tables
rubrics_metrics.description: '..' indicates either zero, not available, or not applicable in the statistical tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe notation conventions and table footnotes when extracting or reusing tabulated data. Consult source references (WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024) for clarification.
